topic: Finding and fixing the count-on error in addition within 10

traps.desc: counted the start number 5 as the first count, landing one short

problems.desc: Student tells why Jen's count went wrong: she said the start number 5 as her first count, so she only counted on 2 hops instead of 3; the count should be 6, 7, 8.

traps.desc: started the count at 6 instead of counting on after it, landing one short

problems.desc: Student finds Kim's mistake: her count 6, 7, 8 used the start number 6 as a hop, so the right count is 7, 8, 9 and the sum is 9.

traps.desc: said 8 as the first hop instead of starting the hops after 8

problems.desc: Student tells how Raj should count: say 8 first without counting it, then hop 9, 10 --- two hops for the 2 being added.

traps.desc: counted the start number as a hop, one short of the true sum

problems.desc: Student checks Ava's claim by counting on from 5 (6, 7, 8, 9), says she is not right, and fixes her sum to 9.
Student tells how saying the start number first, before any hops, stops the count-on mistake: the hops then match the number being added, for example 6 then 7, 8, 9 for the 3 hops.
problems.slot: tell how it stops the mistake
